chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz, from Ayub ibn Nuh, all of them from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The divorce of the pregnant woman is one (revocation), and her waiting period is until she gives birth to her child, and that is the nearer of the two periods.'

key_terms.تَضَعُ حَمْلَهَا: She gives birth to her child

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (Iddah) for a pregnant woman who is divorced according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the iddah of a pregnant woman concludes upon delivery, a ruling derived directly from the Quran but further specified in Shia jurisprudence to ensure the child's lineage is clear. This narration emphasizes that the waiting period is singular and definitive, distinguishing it from the dual-period structure applied to non-pregnant women, thereby highlighting the practical wisdom of aligning legal timelines with biological reality.
